title: The Flax

full_text:
The flax plant bloomed in the meadow with delicate blue flowers like the sky. "I am the happiest of plants!" sang the flax. "The sun warms me, the rain refreshes me, and I shall be made into fine linen!"

One day, workers pulled the flax by the roots, steeped it in water, broke it on the brake, and carded it with iron teeth. "Ouch! This is painful!" cried the flax. "Yet one must suffer to become useful."

It was spun into delicate white thread and woven into fine linen tablecloths for the royal palace. "How splendid!" rejoiced the flax. "I am useful to mankind!"

Years passed. The linen wore into rags. It was torn, boiled in lye, and beaten into pulp at the paper mill. From its fibers was created glorious white paper upon which inspiring stories were printed!

Finally, the paper was cast into the hearth. As it burned, thousands of bright sparks danced like children up the chimney into the golden sun, singing: "The song is never done! Life ascends forever into light!"
moral: Every painful dissolution is the doorway to a higher, more glorious state of service.
